tagline: Sandstone ranges of lookouts, waterfalls and rock art, 260 km west of Melbourne
description: Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park covers about 167,000 ha of uplifted sandstone ranges at the western end of the Great Dividing Range, with Mount William the highest point at 1,167 m. Halls Gap is the only town and main access point, and the Wonderland area beside it is the most popular for day walks. The park holds about 90% of Victoria's Aboriginal rock art, and Brambuk, the cultural centre at Halls Gap, is owned and managed by Jardwadjali and Djab Wurrung people. About a third of Victoria's flora grows here, including more than 75 orchid species.
whyVisit: Walk to lookouts over the ranges
See Aboriginal rock art in Gariwerd
Find wildflowers and orchids in spring
Spot kangaroos and emus at Halls Gap

goodToKnow.title: Check track closures
goodToKnow.detail: The 2024-25 fires burned over 135,000 ha and damaged tracks and camps. Check Parks Victoria for open sites before you go.

goodToKnow.title: Walk in winter or spring
goodToKnow.detail: Summer in the ranges can be very hot and dry. Winter and spring are the best seasons for walking.

goodToKnow.title: Stay at Halls Gap
goodToKnow.detail: The only town in the park, with the supermarket, visitor centre and Wonderland walks beside it. Kangaroos graze nearby in late afternoon.

tagline: Limestone stacks, arches and gorges on the Great Ocean Road's Shipwreck Coast
description: Port Campbell National Park protects about 1,750 ha of limestone coast between Peterborough and Princetown, roughly 190 km south-west of Melbourne. The Southern Ocean has carved sheer cliffs, offshore stacks, gorges, arches and blowholes, and erosion that cut caves, then arches, left the Twelve Apostles standing. The clipper Loch Ard was wrecked here in 1878 and only two of the 54 aboard survived. Little penguins can sometimes be seen at dusk, and short-tailed shearwaters return to Mutton Bird Island between October and April.
whyVisit: See the Twelve Apostles rise from the sea
Look for whales and penguins on the coast
Follow clifftop lookouts along the coast

goodToKnow.title: Stay in Port Campbell
goodToKnow.detail: There is no accommodation or camping in the park, and sleeping in car parks is prohibited. The nearest beds are in Port Campbell or Warrnambool.

goodToKnow.title: Don't swim here
goodToKnow.detail: The water is cold even in summer and the beaches are unsuitable for swimming or surfing, so enjoy them from the sand.

goodToKnow.title: Come at dusk for penguins
goodToKnow.detail: Penguins are best seen in summer just after sunset near the Twelve Apostles and London Bridge. Sightings are not guaranteed.
